examples.text: Этот Спартак даже тут играть не умеет.
examples.trans: This Spartak does not even know how to play here.

examples.text: Нужно поехать туда и собрать кроватку.
examples.trans: You need to go there and assemble the crib.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне кажется, там кто-то есть.
examples.trans: It seems to me someone is over there.

examples.text: Мне тоже казалось, что шеф наблюдает.
examples.trans: It seemed to me too that the chef was watching.

examples.text: Этот Спартак даже тут играть не умеет.
examples.trans: This Spartak does not even know how to play here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Их просто в мусорку выкинут.
examples.trans: They will simply throw them in the trash.

examples.text: Завтра её из роддома выписывают.
examples.trans: Tomorrow she is being discharged from the maternity hospital.

examples.text: Завтра утром моих девчонок выписывают из роддома.
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning my girls are being discharged from the hospital.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'даваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'was letting win'.

related.gloss: not to was letting win (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и поддаваться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and was letting win on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют поддаваться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to was letting win.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'open', paired with 'открыть'.

examples.text: Открывай дверь, это Тимур с кроваткой!
examples.trans: Open the door, that is Timur with the crib!

examples.text: Я сейчас буду открывать.
examples.trans: I'm going to open it now.

examples.text: Магазин открывают в девять.
examples.trans: They open the shop at nine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ведь это настоящее воровство.
examples.trans: After all, this is real theft.

examples.text: Вот у Сени — это воровство.
examples.trans: Now what Senya does—that is theft.

examples.text: Попробуй сама, как это вкусно.
examples.trans: Taste for yourself how delicious it is.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Айнура, так делать совсем нельзя.
examples.trans: Ainura, we really should not do this.

examples.text: Ведь это настоящее воровство.
examples.trans: After all, this is real theft.

examples.text: Вот у Сени — это воровство.
examples.trans: Now what Senya does—that is theft.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'baby crib' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нужно поехать туда и собрать кроватку.
examples.trans: You need to go there and assemble the crib.

examples.text: Папа, собери кроватку, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Dad, assemble the crib, please.

examples.text: Ты хоть кроватку для ребёнка собрал?
examples.trans: Have you even assembled the crib for the baby?
